Imagine a long, long time ago, people called Vikings were sailing and living in places like Scandinavia and England. Now, you asked about “dwarf colonies.” When grown-ups talk about “dwarves,” they usually mean little people from stories and myths, like in fairy tales or movies, not real people.

But if you mean “dwarf” as in people with a condition that makes them very short (like what we now call achondroplasia), here’s the simple answer:

There are no special groups or “colonies” of very short people (dwarves in the real-life sense) that we know of from the Viking Age. But there were probably a few people who were very short because of how they were born, just like there are a few short people today. However, we don’t have any special records or stories about a whole group of very short people living together during the Viking Age.

So, there are no real “dwarf colonies” from the Viking time that we know about. Most stories about dwarves are from fairy tales and myths, not real history.
